title: fix: lower GPT-5.6 Luna price
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Lowers `gpt-5.6-luna`'s price multiplier from `0.5` to `0.2`; routing, aliases, access, capabilities, and fallback remain unchanged.
- Matches [OpenAI's current Luna pricing](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing): $0.20/M input, $0.02/M cached input, $0.25/M cache write, and $1.20/M output; long-context pricing is $0.40/$0.04/$0.50/$1.80.
- Keeps the existing Azure OpenAI East US deployment `gpt-5.6-luna`, Quest-Pollen access, and no fallback. Azure is still billing its older sheet, so Pollinations absorbs the difference until Azure updates.
- Updates only the existing multiplier assertions and effective-price snapshot.
- Verified 376 focused pricing/alias tests, Gen model-catalog tests, canonical plus both aliases, text/image inputs, tools, streaming, cache MISS/HIT, Quest-only billing, unauthorized rejection, and a 5-request burst. Tinybird confirmed Azure, no fallback, and exact `0.2` cost-to-price ratios.

gist.headline: Luna got lighter
gist.blurb: The Luna price tag shed some unnecessary weight. GPT-5.6 Luna now costs 0.2× instead of 0.5×, while its routes, aliases, Quest access, and Azure deployment keep calmly doing their thing.
gist.summary: Updated the `gpt-5.6-luna` price multiplier from `0.5` to `0.2`, matching OpenAI's current Luna pricing while preserving the existing Azure East US deployment, aliases, Quest-Pollen access, and no-fallback behavior.
gist.impact: GPT-5.6 Luna requests now receive the lower 0.2× cost-to-price ratio across text, image inputs, tools, streaming, and cache states, with the same model access and routing as before.
gist.visual_concept: A cozy night garden market where Polli carefully replaces a heavy 0.5 price weight with a small 0.2 weight beside a glowing Luna moon terminal. The terminal represents the unchanged Azure deployment and shows a stable route line; code-plants and small flowers make the lower price feel like a useful bit of pruning rather than a dramatic event.
